name: Lenskart Solutions Ltd
title: Lenskart Solutions Ltd - 544600 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Lenskart is a retail eyewear story with store growth and same-store sales driving volume, but there is no supply-discipline signal: management is accelerating store adds (455 net new in nine months) and capex, so the capital-cycle read is expansionary.

triggers.quote: In nine months, we added 455 net new stores, the fastest expansion in our history

triggers.label: India SSSG 18.3%, eye tests +42.7%
triggers.quote: Same store sales growth was 18.3%, broad -based across tiers

triggers.label: International EBITDA margin 10.6%
triggers.quote: EBITDA pre-Ind AS 116 margin reached 10.6%, up from 4.5% last year

summary.headline: Lenskart Q1 FY27 revenue grew 34% YoY and PAT rose 182% to ₹228 crore, with India same-store sales growth at 18.3%.
summary.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue up 34% YoY and PAT up 182% to ₹228 crore, against full-year FY26 PAT of about ₹530 crore. India revenue grew 30.7% to ₹1,531 crore with pre-Ind AS 116 EBITDA margin of 15.4%, while International revenue grew 38% to ₹1,203 crore with pre-Ind AS 116 EBITDA margin of 10.6%. Store network expansion was the fastest in company history at 455 net new stores over nine months, and the company framed its growth around densification and entry into unserved pin codes. Figures are on a proforma basis, which matched reported figures for the quarter.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹1,531 crore (+30.7%); product margin 64.2%; marketing 4.8% of revenue (from 5.7%); SSSG 18.3%, same pin code sales growth 24%; eye tests 63 lakh (+42.7%); eyewear units 82 lakh (+22.8%); 116 net new stores and 50 new cities added.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹1,203 crore (+38%); product margin 77.1%; eyewear units +37.6%, transacting customers +27.8%, eye tests +20.5%, sunglasses units +58.4%; only 16 net new stores added in the quarter.

guidance_outlook: Management expects International store additions to accelerate in some markets, but said acceleration is more likely in coming years than this year, pending tech integration.
Management said India can support materially more stores (over 6,100 pin codes unserved; densification allows at least another 3,000 stores; India points past 10,000 stores).
Management said it expects Y-o-Y margin improvement in International through FY27 but declined to guide the full-year margin against Q1, which benefits from seasonal sunglasses sales.
Management said short-term currency headwinds could persist if the currency weakens further; product margin offset is expected to improve with Hyderabad plant and insourcing.
capex_capacity: Q1 store capex ₹75 crore and plant capex ₹132 crore, mainly for the Hyderabad facility.
Remote optometry live in 786 stores (up from 168 at FY25 end).
Self AI eye test entered pilot stores; B by Lenskart live with 80,000+ sign-ups and a few hundred glasses shipping daily.
Manufacturing of branded lenses (Rodenstock, Tokai) in India, with plans to extend to international markets.
demand_pricing: Same store sales growth 18.3% in India vs 16% a year earlier; same pin code sales growth 24% (SPSG corrected to 24.3%).
Store density in 1,517 existing pin codes rose from 1.5 to 1.6 stores over nine months; Bangalore SSSG about 20%.
Launched ₹500 eyewear with lenses and warranty via Hustlr Club; premium lenses above ₹30,000 generating about ₹250 crore annually.
Owndays prescription eyeglasses sales over ₹1,500 crore; China market growing about 13% CAGR cited as reference.
Management said ASP can fluctuate quarter to quarter and that lower price points are more margin accretive in absolute rupees.

qa_highlights.question: Will store expansion from ~2,700 to ~10,000 stores hurt same-store sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said densification has not diluted SSSG; penetration is about 35%, and the company is adding new price bands below ₹1,000 and above ₹10,000. It said eye test volume is the funnel driver and that supply-side engineering is the constraint.

qa_highlights.question: Is gross margin resilience a sign that currency concerns are less elevated?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said a large part of revenue is non-INR, giving a natural hedge; product margin was protected by in-house frame manufacturing, vendor volume discounts and mix, but short-term headwinds could persist if the currency weakens.

qa_highlights.question: What is the biggest long-term constraint to the vision: product, real estate or talent?
qa_highlights.answer: Peyush Bansal said talent, especially engineering talent able to apply data and AI, is the main constraint as the company scales.

qa_highlights.question: Why did SSSG, SPSG and NPS moderate, and has NPS recovered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the NPS dip to confusion over social media communication about policies, said it has been clarified and NPS is back near earlier levels, and said SSSG rose from 16% a year ago to 18%.

qa_highlights.question: What share of eye test customers buy glasses and how many bring outside prescriptions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a significant majority of eye test customers buy glasses, immediately or within months; first-time customers convert slower. It did not give a percentage for outside prescriptions.

qa_highlights.question: Is the International Q1 margin a fair guide for full-year FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said FY26 International EBITDA margin (post-rent) was about 7%, Q1 benefits from seasonally higher-margin sunglasses, and management aims for Y-o-Y improvement but would not guide the full-year margin.

risks_watch: Currency: product margin benefited from hedging and sourcing actions, but further INR movement could weigh on margins.
Store productivity: rapid store additions could dilute same store sales and NPS; NPS dip was attributed to a policy communication issue.
Conversion risk: rising first-time eye tests may lower conversion from eye tests to purchases, per management.
International expansion pace remains slow (16 net new stores in the quarter), with tech integration gating acceleration.
Talent and engineering capacity flagged by management as the most important constraint to the expansion plan.
Accuracy of remote optometry and self eye test; no defined accuracy metric yet, with exchange-for-power-change tracking as a proxy.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth, store runway and the long-term vision; more measured and evasive on international margin guidance, currency and specific metrics such as outside prescription share.
key_quotes: Demand is being added, not divided.
In our business, growth and profitability are positively correlated.
The key here will be supply.
Talent and the culture, the speed of operation.

financial_highlights.value: above 70% (first time after four quarters at ~69%)

financial_highlights.change: margin up from 4.5%; amount ~3x last year

adds.what: Hyderabad lens manufacturing plant (plant capex ₹132 crore in Q1, largely for Hyderabad facility)
Net new stores: 455 added over nine months, 116 India and 16 International in Q1 (store capex ₹75 crore in Q1)
India store densification: at least another 3,000 stores possible, path past 10,000 stores (no timeline given)
International store additions to accelerate in some markets, more likely in coming years pending tech integration (no number or timeline given)

growth.why: No explicit full-year revenue guidance given; management points to strong Q1 growth (revenue +34%, India SSSG 18.3%) and runway for 3,000+ more India stores via densification, backed by 455 net new stores in nine months and ₹132 crore Hyderabad plant capex, though store timing and International acceleration are not quantified.
